title: CoreWeave Tees Up First India Data Centers With AdaniConneX Deal
source_used: The Next Web (relays CoreWeave's announcement and Bloomberg's figure)
key_facts: CoreWeave, described as a US AI cloud provider, announced the deal on Wednesday 7 Oct 2026 to open its first data centres in India.

The data centres use 240 MW of capacity at an AdaniConneX campus in Navi Mumbai; CoreWeave is the only tenant across three 80 MW buildings at the Taloja campus, with an option for up to another 240 MW.
CoreWeave expects the first phase to come online in mid-2028 and plans to install Nvidia's Vera Rubin platform.
Bloomberg reported that the investment will total multiple billions of dollars; CoreWeave did not give a figure in its statement.
AdaniConneX is a 50:50 joint venture between Adani Enterprises and EdgeConneX.
CoreWeave will open an office in India, hire local staff, and linked the investment to the government's IndiaAI Mission.
CoreWeave rents GPU computing (graphics chips used for AI) to AI companies; such providers are known as neoclouds.
India is CoreWeave's second market in Asia, after its August announcement of data centre projects in Indonesia.
quote_evidence: "India has the talent, developers, and ambition to become a major center of AI innovation," said Sachin Jain, CoreWeave's chief operating officer.
CoreWeave did not give a figure in its statement.
The investment will total multiple billions of dollars over the life of the project, Bloomberg reported.
why_it_matters_hint: Adds AI computing capacity in India, linked to the government's AI programme; the company gave no investment figure.
